title: Compact cohort railway for staged traffic and autonomous rollback
author: Zara Patel
release_notes: Introduce compact cohort railway orchestration for staged traffic routing with autonomous rollback heuristics and telemetry gates. Backwards compatible runtime flags and opt-in policy config for managed/private deployments.
description: Motivation: We need a lightweight staged-rollout primitive that fits in constrained Dedicated/Private environments and reduces blast radius while preserving session coherence and fast rollback. The Compact Cohort Railway (CCR) is a small-footprint controller and routing adapter that advances cohorts through lanes (shadow->mini-canary->canary->promote) with telemetry-anchored gates and an autonomous rollback oracle. This PR implements CCR as an opt-in orchestration mode for the deployment controller, includes heuristics for autonomy thresholds, and provides an ops playbook and smoke-suite. Design notes: 1) Cohorts are fixed-size buckets assigned at client-session start to preserve stickiness. 2) Each lane includes a short-lived shadow replication path for fidelity checks and a latency SLO probe. 3) Progression rules are delta-based and evaluate latency, error-rate, and a small prompt-quality embedding drift metric computed with a compact eval set. 4) Autonomous rollback uses a conservative grace-window and requires either crossing delta thresholds or a sustained uplift in error signals; operators can also attach manual holdpoints. 5) For Private deployments CCR runs in a single binary with a lightweight local memory ledger, for Hosted/Dedicated it integrates with existing rollout store. Checklist: - [x] Controller implementation (railway state machine) - [x] Routing adapter for session-coherent bucket assignment - [x] Telemetry gates and compact eval pipeline - [x] Autorevert oracle with grace-window and audit logs - [x] End-to-end smoke tests and chaos scenario - [x] Docs and operator playbook - [x] Metrics + dashboards scoped to per-cohort view Backwards compatibility and opt-in: CCR is disabled by default; the rollout API accepts rollout.mode="compact_cohort" and rollout.policy references an existing policy document. No existing routes change unless customers flip the flag. Related work: builds on rollout-saga primitives in ENG-4034 and shadow-verifier work in ENG-2291. Implementation summary: commits below change the controller state machine, add a compact in-memory ledger, extend routing middleware to honor cohort cookies, add a small eval job that computes embedding drift and wire telemetry, and add docs and smoke-tests. Security and perf: ledger uses signed checkpoints to avoid tampering; memory footprint tested against 10k concurrent sessions with <120MB overhead. Rollout behavior is rate-limited to avoid sudden capacity pressure. Operational playbook excerpt: 1) Enable CCR on a staging fleet with 5% cohort size. 2) Monitor per-cohort latency/error and embedding drift dashboard. 3) If autonomous rollback triggers, follow the audit trail in /rollouts/ledger and optionally replay the cohort. 4) To force promote, use the CLI promote --cohort <id>. Links: design doc https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2291/compact-cohort-railway design-tests https://git.internal/redwood/ci/pipeline/CCR-smoke, runbook https://confluence.redwood/ops/CCR-playbook.

ci_checks: build: pass, unit-tests: pass, e2e-smoke: pass, lint: pass (rerun after fix), security-scan: pass
ops_impact: Adds a new rollout.mode option and introduces per-cohort metrics. Operators should add cohort capacity panels. Minimal infra change for Private: local ledger persisted under /var/lib/redwood/ccr-ledger unless disabled.
notes_for_release: Enable by opt-in only. Recommend incubating in staging for 2 weeks before Dedicated rollout. Watch for embedding-drift false positives and tune eval set per product.
qa_summary: E2E smoke tested with staged promote/rollback scenarios, chaos injection to simulate slow nodes, and performance validation under 10k concurrent sessions. No regressions observed in default rollout flow.
playbook_snippet: If autonomous rollback fires: 1) check /ops/rollouts/ccr/ledger for cohort id and events 2) if false positive, run replay --cohort <id> --dry-run to validate 3) to revert permanently run rollout abort --cohort <id>
